configVersion = 4

#Frontier settings.

	[frontier.announcement]
		#Announce unnamed frontiers in chat/title.
		announceUnnamed = false

		[frontier.announcement.title]
			#Duration of title announcement, in game ticks.
			#Range: 0 ~ 1200
			duration = 70
			#Minimum time between consecutive title announcement, in game ticks.
			#Range: 0 ~ 1200
			timeout = 0
			#Show the frontier announcement above the hotbar instead of showing it as a title.
			aboveHotbar = false

	[frontier.editing]
		#Distance at which vertices snap to nearby vertices.
		#Range: 0 ~ 16
		snapDistance = 8

	[frontier.appearance]
		#Hide frontier names when they do not fit at the current zoom level.
		hideNamesThatDontFit = false

		[frontier.appearance.fill]
			#Transparency of the frontier fill. 0.0 is fully transparent and 1.0 is opaque.
			#Range: 0.0 ~ 1.0
			opacity = 0.4

		[frontier.appearance.border]
			#Width of the frontier border.
			#Range: 0 ~ 64
			width = 0
			#Transparency of the frontier border. 0.0 is fully transparent and 1.0 is opaque.
			#Range: 0.0 ~ 1.0
			opacity = 1.0

		[frontier.appearance.pathMarkers]
			#Size of path markers.
			#Range: 1 ~ 5
			size = 2
			#Transparency of path markers. 0.0 is fully transparent and 1.0 is opaque.
			#Range: 0.0 ~ 1.0
			opacity = 1.0

		[frontier.appearance.text]
			#Size of the frontier text.
			#Range: 1 ~ 5
			size = 2
			#Transparency of the frontier text. 0.0 is fully transparent and 1.0 is opaque.
			#Range: 0.0 ~ 1.0
			opacity = 1.0
			#Color of the frontier text. FrontierColor uses the frontier color. FrontierColorBright uses the same color at maximum brightness.
			#Allowed Values: FrontierColor, FrontierColorBright, White
			color = "FrontierColor"

		[frontier.appearance.banner]
			#Size of the frontier banner.
			#Range: 1 ~ 5
			size = 1
			#Transparency of the frontier banner. 0.0 is fully transparent and 1.0 is opaque.
			#Range: 0.0 ~ 1.0
			opacity = 1.0

	[frontier.default]
		#Default first name line for new frontiers.
		name1 = "New"
		#Default second name line for new frontiers.
		name2 = "Frontier"
		#Use a random color for new frontiers by default.
		randomColor = true
		#Fallback fixed color for new frontiers when random color is disabled.
		#Format: "RRGGBB". Also accepts "#RRGGBB", "0xRRGGBB", and "0xAARRGGBB".

				#Default title announcement visibility for new frontiers.

	#Change the foliage colour based on the current season
	change_foliage_color = true
	#Change the grass color based on the current season
	change_grass_color = true
	#Change the birch colour based on the current season
	change_birch_color = true

	#Seasons will only apply to dimensons listed here
	whitelisted_dimensions = ["minecraft:overworld"]

	#Change the frequency of rain/snow/storms based on the season
	change_weather_frequency = true
	#Generate snow and ice during the Winter season
	generate_snow_ice = true

	#0 = Random, 1 - 3 = Early/Mid/Late Spring
	#4 - 6 = Early/Mid/Late Summer
	#7 - 9 = Early/Mid/Late Autumn
	#10 - 12 = Early/Mid/Late Winter
	starting_sub_season = 1

	#This only adjusts the internal length of a day used by the season cycle.
	#It is intended to be used in conjunction with another mod which adjusts the actual length of a Minecraft day.
	day_duration = 24000

configs.sound_physics_remastered/soundphysics.pr:
# Enables/Disables all sound effects
enabled=true
# Affects how quiet a sound gets based on distance
# Lower values mean distant sounds are louder
# This setting requires you to be in singleplayer or having the mod installed on the server
# 1.0 is the physically correct value
attenuation_factor=1.0
# The ray distance at which reverb starts
# 0.0 disables reverb attenuation
reverb_attenuation_distance=0.0
# The volume of simulated reverberations
reverb_gain=1.0
# The brightness of reverberation
# Higher values result in more high frequencies in reverberation
# Lower values give a more muffled sound to the reverb
reverb_brightness=1.0
# The distance of reverb relative to the sound distance
reverb_distance=1.5
# The amount of sound that will be absorbed when traveling through blocks
block_absorption=1.0
# Higher values mean smaller objects won't be considered as occluding
occlusion_variation=0.35
# The default amount of sound reflectance energy for all blocks
# Lower values result in more conservative reverb simulation with shorter reverb tails
# Higher values result in more generous reverb simulation with higher reverb tails
default_block_reflectivity=0.5
# The default amount of occlusion for all blocks
# Lower values will result in sounds being less muffled through walls
# Higher values mean sounds will be not audible though thicker walls
default_block_occlusion_factor=1.0
# Minecraft won't allow sounds to play past a certain distance
# This parameter is a multiplier for how far away a sound source is allowed to be in order for it to actually play
# This setting only takes affect in singleplayer worlds and when installed on the server
sound_distance_allowance=4.0
# A value controlling the amount that air absorbs high frequencies with distance
# A value of 1.0 is physically correct for air with normal humidity and temperature
# Higher values mean air will absorb more high frequencies with distance
# 0 disables this effect
air_absorption=1.0
# How much sound is filtered when the player is underwater
# 0.0 means no filter
# 1.0 means fully filtered
underwater_filter=0.9
# Whether sounds like cave, nether or underwater ambient sounds should have sound physics
evaluate_ambient_sounds=false
# The number of rays to trace to determine reverberation for each sound source
# More rays provides more consistent tracing results but takes more time to calculate
# Decrease this value if you experience lag spikes when sounds play
environment_evaluation_ray_count=32
# The number of rays bounces to trace to determine reverberation for each sound source
# More bounces provides more echo and sound ducting but takes more time to calculate
# Decrease this value if you experience lag spikes when sounds play
environment_evaluation_ray_bounces=4
# If sound hits a non-full-square side, block occlusion is multiplied by this
non_full_block_occlusion_factor=0.25
# The maximum amount of rays to determine occlusion
# Directly correlates to the amount of blocks between walls that are considered
max_occlusion_rays=16
# The amount at which occlusion is capped
max_occlusion=64.0
# If enabled, the occlusion calculation only uses one path between the sound source and the listener instead of 9
strict_occlusion=false
# Whether to try calculating where the sound should come from based on reflections
sound_direction_evaluation=true
# Skip redirecting non-occluded sounds (the ones you can see directly)
redirect_non_occluded_sounds=true
# If music discs or other longer sounds should be frequently reevaluated
update_moving_sounds=false
# The interval in ticks that moving sounds are reevaluated
# Lower values mean more frequent reevaluation but also more lag
# This option only takes effect if update_moving_sounds is enabled
sound_update_interval=5
# The maximum distance a sound can be processed
max_sound_processing_distance=512.0
# Disable level clone and cache. This will fall back to original main thread access.
# WARNING! Enabling this will cause instability and issues with other mods.
unsafe_level_access=false
# The radius of chunks to clone for level access
level_clone_range=4
# The maximum number of ticks to retain the cloned level in the cache
level_clone_max_retain_ticks=20
# The maximum distance a player can move from the cloned origin before invalidation
level_clone_max_retain_block_distance=16
# Enables debug logging
debug_logging=false
# Provides more information about occlusion in the logs
occlusion_logging=false
# Provides more information about the environment calculation in the logs
environment_logging=false
# Provides more information about how long computations take
performance_logging=false
# If enabled, the path of the sound will be rendered in game
render_sound_bounces=false
# If enabled, occlusion will be visualized in game
render_occlusion=false
# Enables/Disables sound effects for Simple Voice Chat audio
simple_voice_chat_integration=true
# Enables/Disables hearing your own echo with Simple Voice Chat
simple_voice_chat_hear_self=true

# Streams Reflowing -- client settings (particles and sounds). Plain key=value; edits apply at once.

# ===================== SOUNDS =====================

# How loud running water sounds. Streams murmur nearby; waterfalls carry.
# 0 = silent, 1 = normal, 2 = loud. Rides the Ambient volume slider.
# Applies at once.
waterAmbience=1.0

# ===================== PARTICLES =====================

# Bubbles riding the current, and splashes where water drops.
# 0 = off, 1 = bubbles that fade in place (cheapest), 2 = bubbles that flow downstream.
# Applies at once.
streamBubbles=2

# With Effective, Particular or Subtle Effects installed: this mod places their waterfall foam at
# the feet of its own waterfalls, and their own waterfall detection is switched off on stream water.
# false = this mod and they each do their own thing.
# Applies at once.
partnerParticles=true

# Whose foam shows at the foot of a waterfall while that integration is on.
# 0 = none, 1 = Effective's, Particular's and Subtle Effects', 2 = this mod's, 3 = both.
# Only matters with Effective, Particular or Subtle Effects installed.
# Applies at once.
waterfallFoam=3

# Sticks and leaves drifting downstream on the surface.
# Applies at once.
streamDebris=true

# How big each droplet of spray is (multiplier).
# Applies at once.
particleSize=1.0

# How much spray is thrown (multiplier).
# Applies at once.
particleDensity=1.0

# Cap on stream particles spawned per tick. Lower it if streams cost frames.
# Applies at once.
maxStreamParticlesPerTick=1000

# How far (blocks) waterfalls are looked for, to spray from a distance.
# 0 = only nearby falls spray.
# Applies at once.
streamParticleScanRadius=256

# Spray on vanilla waterfalls too, not only this mod's streams.
# Applies at once.
particlesOnVanillaWater=true

# ===================== OTHER =====================

# Show the Streams Reflowing progress line on the world-loading screen.
# Applies at once.
loadingNotice=true
configs.streamsreflowing.properties:
# Streams Reflowing -- settings (this file: the world side; streamsreflowing-client.properties: particles and sounds).
# Plain key=value. Edit and save: most settings apply at once; the rest say when they apply.
# layout: 2.14 text 50ff902a

# ===================== PERFORMANCE & STREAM PLANNING =====================
# Accuracy level sets how much work new land costs. Watershed size sets how long each pause is.
# Land is planned once and saved with the world, so the cost is paid one time per area.

# Carve this mod's streams into new land.
# false = no streams anywhere (lakes and currents still work).
# Applies to newly generated land only.
generateStreams=true

# Fill the basins this mod finds with lakes.
# false = no lakes from this mod.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
generateLakes=true

# Multiplayer: let players' own games prepare the streams for the land they explore, so the server does less.
# Only players who have this mod help; everyone else is served by the server as usual.
# Helpers are sent this world's seed. Applies at once.
offloadRegionBuilds=false

# On a server that asks, let this game prepare the streams for the land you explore.
# It uses spare processor time while you travel. false = the server does it all.
# Applies when you next join a server.
helpPrepareRegions=true

# How many areas this game prepares for a server at the same time (1 to 3).
# Lower it if helping costs you frames while you travel.
# Applies when you next join a server.
helpRegionsAtOnce=3

# How finely the land is read to plan streams. Higher = closer to the terrain, more work per area.
# EXTREME and MAX cost far more: pre-generate. How many streams there are is growDensity and wetness.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
terrainAccuracyLevel=MEDIUM

# Blocks across one stream system. Bigger = longer, wider streams and fewer seams.
# Performance: same total work in bigger pieces. Double the size = pauses 4x longer, 4x rarer.
# New worlds only: a world keeps the size it was started with.
watershedSize=BLOCKS_768

# How far a vanilla river's current is planned, as a multiple of the watershed.
# 1 = one watershed (default), 2 = twice, 3 = four times. Larger finds far outlets, costs more.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
riverDrainageSize=1

# How closely each stream hugs the land after its course is planned.
# 4 = closest, 2 = lighter, 0 = none, -1 = follow the accuracy level.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
terrainFit=-1

# Read the land in full where it bends (valleys, ridges, peaks) instead of estimating it.
# Streams follow rugged land more truly, at more work there. false = faster.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
adaptiveGridRead=true

# Estimate the height of the land where the estimate has proved accurate, instead of reading it in full.
# Much faster on terrain it suits. false = every height is read in full.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
fastTerrainEstimate=true

# Put stream and lake sample points on the terrain's 4-block grid, where the land is cheapest to read.
# Faster world generation; a point can sit up to 2 blocks from where it would otherwise. false = exact spots.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
alignReadPoints=true

# Place streams the way versions before 2.14 did.
# For comparing, or to keep new land in step with an older world.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
legacyStreamShaping=false

# Load chunks faster on packs that generate chunks in parallel.
# No effect otherwise. Turn off only if chunk loading misbehaves.
# Applies at once.
fastChunkLoading=true

# ----- Where streams may go -----

# Biomes where no stream starts and no lake forms on its own.
# A stream that starts elsewhere still runs through them.
# Comma-separated ids, #tags, or modid:* wildcards.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing worlds keep cutting streams off at these biomes.
streamBiomeBlacklist=terrestria:caldera,terrestria:canyon

# Biomes a stream may end in (its mouth).
# Comma-separated biome #tags or ids.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
outletBiomes=#minecraft:is_river,#minecraft:is_ocean,#c:is_swamp

# Follow ReTerraForged's terrain and rivers when that mod is installed.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
reterraforgedCompat=true

# Experimental: let a stream that peters out search for another stream to join.
# Costs more planning at region borders.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
connectNearbyWater=false

# How far (blocks) a dead end searches when connectNearbyWater is on.
# -1 = automatic.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
connectRadius=-1

# ----- Stream appearance: how many, how long, how they branch -----

# How much water the land carries. Above 1 = more streams, wider streams, more planning work.
# 1.0 is the default. Below 1 = fewer headwaters and narrower streams.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
wetnessMultiplier=1.0

# How much of the usual water the driest climates keep.
# 0 = none, 0.1 = a tenth (default), 1 = as much as anywhere.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
wetnessDryFloor=0.1

# How finely streams branch. Lower = more small tributaries, and more planning work.
# 0.75 is the default; 2.0 is the sparsest.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
growDensity=0.75

# The shortest stream, in blocks, allowed from its source to the water it reaches.
# 0 = keep every stream. Dry biomes are always exempt.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
minStreamLength=75

# Which water the shortest-stream rule applies to.
# 1 = the ocean, 2 = ocean and rivers, 3 = ocean, rivers and lakes.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
minLengthScope=2

# The smallest basin (blocks of water surface) that becomes a lake.
# A deep pit in the path of a stream fills as a plunge pool whatever its size.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
lakeMinArea=1024.0

# The largest lake allowed (blocks of water surface). 0 = automatic.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
lakeMaxArea=0.0

# ----- Stream appearance: width, depth and winding -----

# How wide streams get for the land that drains into them.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
widthScale=1.0

# How thin a stream starts at its source (half-width, blocks).
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
baseWidth=0.4

# The widest a stream can get (half-width, blocks).
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
maxWidth=16.0

# How much streams wind. Steep reaches straighten on their own.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
meanderStrength=1.2

# How deep the stream bed sits below the water, as a fraction of stream width.
# 0.24 = about a quarter (default). Higher = deeper, steeper channels.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
streamDepth=0.24

# Steep reaches run narrower, flat reaches spread wider.
# 0 = off, 1 = full effect.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
widthFollowsSlope=0.5

# Wet biomes carry wider streams, dry biomes narrower.
# 0 = off, 1 = full effect.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
widthFollowsClimate=0.5

# Streams pinch and broaden along their course.
# 0 = off, 1 = full effect.
# Takes effect in new worlds. Existing land keeps its streams.
widthVariation=0.5

# Steep, firm-banked reaches cut deeper; flat sandy ones run shallow.
# 0 = off, 1 = full effect.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
depthFollowsTerrain=0.5

# Bends run deep on the outer bank with a gravel shelf on the inside.
# 0 = off, 1 = full effect.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
bendAsymmetry=0.5

# Flat, loose-banked reaches run shallow and braided around bars.
# 0 = off, 1 = full effect.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
channelBars=0.5

# Flat, loose-banked streams fan out where they meet the sea or a lake.
# 0 = off, 1 = full effect.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
deltaMouths=0.5

# Keep stream water in its channel where it crosses a slope.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
containmentBerm=true

# How ragged the bank edges are (blocks of jitter, 0 to 3).
# Applies to newly generated land only.
bankNoise=0.21

# ----- Stream appearance: banks, plants and scenery -----

# Skin the channel with the bank styles in config/streamsreflowing/bank_styles.
# false = raw carved ground.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
customBanks=true

# Bank materials on other water too.
# 0 = this mod's water only, 1 = also rivers, lakes and ponds, 2 = also ocean shores.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
allWaterBanks=1

# Where bank scenery (config/streamsreflowing/bank_features) may appear.
# 0 = nowhere, 1 = this mod's streams, 2 = also its lakes, 3 = every water edge.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
bankFeatures=3

# Extra plants beside this mod's streams.
# 0 = none, 1 = grass and ferns, 2 = also the biome's own plants (biome-boost).
# Applies to newly generated land only.
vegetation=1

# Extra plants beside other water too (rivers, lakes, oceans).
# 0 = off, 1 = grass and ferns, 2 = also biome-boost.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
allWaterFlora=1

# How far (blocks) from the water the extra plants reach.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
floraRadius=5

# How dense the bank grass is at the water's edge (percent).
# Applies to newly generated land only.
bankGrassPercent=20

# How dense the biome-boost plants are at the water's edge (percent).
# Applies to newly generated land only.
biomeBoostPercent=4

# Placed features the biome-boost must never use.
# Comma-separated feature ids.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
biomeBoostBlacklist=

# Seagrass and other water plants on submerged floors.
# 0 = off, 1 = this mod's lakes, 2 = also its streams, 3 = all water.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
underwaterFlora=3

# How dense the underwater plants are (percent).
# Applies to newly generated land only.
underwaterFloraPercent=15

# Biomes that get no underwater plants.
# Comma-separated biome ids or #tags.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
underwaterFloraBiomeBlacklist=

# ----- Stream appearance: river biome marking -----

# Mark carved streams as a river biome, for fish, spawns and water colour.
# 0 = off, 1 = the best matching river biome, 2 = a river biome tinted like the land around it.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
rebiomeStreams=1

# The same for this mod's lakes.
# 0 = off, 1 = the best matching river biome, 2 = a river biome tinted like the land around it.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
rebiomeLakes=1

# ===================== WATER BEHAVIOR: CURRENTS, BOATS, MOBS AND ITEMS =====================
# These affect all water in the world, not just this mod's streams.

# Give streams a downstream current while they stay ordinary water.
# false = streams are still water.
# Applies at once.
vanillaWaterFlow=true

# Give vanilla and terrain-mod rivers one coherent current toward the sea.
# Needs vanillaWaterFlow.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
flowVanillaRivers=true

# Keep a river flowing one way where it crosses between map areas.
# Its direction can then depend on which side you explored first.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
riverSeamAgreement=true

# Water spreads across pool surfaces so streams flow continuously over them.
# false = fully vanilla spreading.
# Applies at once.
spillOverWater=true

# Limit that spreading to water this mod gives a current to.
# false = every water block in the world spills over water.
# Leave on: with it off, other mods' water channels and tanks can overflow.
# Applies at once.
spillOnStreamsOnly=true

# Boats float on flowing stream water instead of sinking.
# Applies at once.
boatsFloatOnFlowingWater=true

# Fish, squid, dolphins and other water mobs hold against the current.
# false = the current carries them too.
# Applies at once.
waterMobsIgnoreFlow=true

# Mobs that always hold position in a current, whatever the automatic rules say.
# Comma-separated entity ids.
# Applies at once.
mobsHoldInCurrent=

# Mobs that always drift with a current, whatever the automatic rules say.
# Comma-separated entity ids.
# Applies at once.
mobsDriftInCurrent=

# How fast a current carries dropped items (blocks per second).
# Applies at once.
itemDriftSpeed=1.5

# How hard flowing water pushes players. 1.0 = the game's own push, 0 = none, up to 4.0.
# Counts for all flowing water, not only this mod's streams.
# On a server, each player's own game decides this for them.
# Applies at once.
playerPush=1.2

# How hard flowing water pushes boats and rafts. 1.0 = the game's own push, 0 = none, up to 4.0.
# Counts for all flowing water, not only this mod's streams.
# On a server, the game of whoever steers the boat decides this.
# Applies at once.
boatPush=2.0

# How hard flowing water pushes mobs and other things. 1.0 = the game's own push, 0 = none, up to 4.0.
# Counts for all flowing water, not only this mod's streams. Dropped items have their own setting.
# Applies at once.
mobPush=1.2

# How fast a current carries Sable physics vessels (blocks per second).
# 0 = off. Only matters with Sable installed.
# Sable Extras applies its own drift too: with it installed you may need to adjust its settings.
# Applies at once.
vesselDriftSpeed=30.0

# ----- Water behavior: other mods' water -----

# The Physics Mod draws its own flowing-water effect over streams.
# 0 = show both, 1 = hide it on streams (its ocean waves stay).
# Applies at once.
physicsModWater=3

# With Flowing Fluids installed, fill streams with this mod's own stream water,
# so they cannot drain away. No effect without that mod.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
bakedFluidWhenFlowingFluids=true

# Always fill streams with this mod's own stream water instead of plain water.
# For setups where other mods drain or displace plain-water streams.
# Applies to newly generated land only.
forceBakedFluid=false

# ===================== PARTICLES & SOUNDS (SERVER SIDE) =====================

# ===================== OTHER =====================

# Show the one-time Streams Reflowing notice in chat when a world is first opened.
# Applies at once.
welcomeMessage=true

# NeoForge and Forge servers: whether players on this server see stream spray and splashes.
# true also turns away players who do not have this mod installed.
# Applies the next time the server starts.
serverStreamParticles=true

    "with neither. At the same level a starred style (star: true) beats the unstarred ones, then a config file beats",
    "a datapack or the mod's own, and among tag styles more tags beat fewer. A tag style needs the biome to carry ALL its tags.",
    "Write tags without #. exclude_biomes and exclude_tags take the style out of the running in those biomes.",
    "This file: 'biomes' takes jungle and sparse jungle over from the mod's own jungle style (a config file beats",
    "the mod at the same level). 'tags' with the star then claims every other jungle, modded ones too, over any other",

    "cohesion: how firmly the banks hold. 0 = loose sand that spreads and forms bars, 1 = clay and roots that keep a",

  "tags": ["minecraft:is_jungle"],
  "exclude_biomes": ["minecraft:bamboo_jungle"],
  "exclude_tags": ["minecraft:is_mountain"],
  "star": true,
  "cohesion": 0.9,
  "bed": ["minecraft:mud", "minecraft:mud", "minecraft:clay"],
  "waterline": { "above": 15, "block": "minecraft:moss_block" },
  "bank": ["minecraft:rooted_dirt", "minecraft:moss_block", "streamsreflowing:chameleon"]
}

    "Every size is a percent of the stream's width, and the reaches ADD UP: 45 + 25 + 20 + 10 fills the whole cut.",

configs.waystones-common.toml:
[blueMap]

# Controls whether Waystones' BlueMap integration should be loaded
enabled = true

# If enabled, sharestones will be tracked as markers on BlueMap.
includeSharestones = true

# If enabled, undiscovered waystones will be tracked as markers on BlueMap.
includeUndiscoveredWaystones = false

# If enabled, waystones will be tracked as markers on BlueMap
includeWaystones = true

[client]

# If enabled, the text overlay on waystones will no longer always render at full brightness.
disableTextGlow = false

[dynmap]

# If enabled, Waystones will add markers for waystones and sharestones to Dynmap.
enabled = true

[inventoryButton]

# The y position of the inventory button in the creative menu.
creativeInventoryButtonX = 88

# The y position of the inventory button in the creative menu.
creativeInventoryButtonY = 33

# Set to 'none' for no inventory button. Set to 'nearest' for an inventory button that teleports to the nearest waystone. Set to 'any' for an inventory button that opens the waystone selection menu. Set to a waystone name for an inventory button that teleports to a specifically named waystone.
inventoryButton = ""

# The x position of the inventory button in the inventory.
inventoryButtonX = 58

# The y position of the inventory button in the inventory.
inventoryButtonY = 60

[journeyMap]

# If enabled, JourneyMap waypoints will be created for each activated waystone.
enabled = true

# If enabled, JourneyMap waypoints will only be created if the mod 'JourneyMap Integration' is not installed
preferJourneyMapIntegrationMod = true

[rules]

# Set to true to allow everyone to manage global waystones. Always true if `defaultVisibility` is `global`. Can be overridden by Shogi Rule `may_manage_global_waystones`.
allowEveryoneToManageGlobalWaystones = false

# Set to "team" or "global" to have newly placed or found waystones use that visibility by default.
defaultVisibility = "activation"

# Set to false to simply disable all cooldowns. See rules for more fine-grained control.
enableCooldowns = true

# Set to false to simply disable all durability costs. See rules for more fine-grained control.
enableDurability = true

# Set to true to enable warp modifier items for applying status effects on teleports.
enableModifiers = true

# Set to false to simply disable all xp costs. See rules for more fine-grained control.
enableXpCosts = true

# List of entities that cannot be teleported, either as pet, leashed, or on warp plates.
entityDenyList = [ "minecraft:wither" ]

# Set to "enabled" to have leashed mobs teleport with you. Set to "same_dimension" to have leashed mobs teleport with you only if you're not changing dimensions. Set to "disabled" to disable.
transportLeashed = "enabled"

# Set to "enabled" to have nearby pets teleport with you. Set to "same_dimension" to have nearby pets teleport with you only if you're not changing dimensions. Set to "disabled" to disable.
transportPets = "disabled"

# List of warp requirements in Shogi format.
warpRequirements = [ 
    "$uses_xp #= and(any(source(is_waystone), source(is_warp_stone)), not(target(is_fleeting_memorial)))", 
    "$uses_xp -> $xp_points_cost = $distance * $xp_per_block", 
    "$uses_xp + is_interdimensional -> $xp_points_cost = $interdimensional_xp_cost", 
    "$uses_xp -> $xp_points_cost = clamp($xp_points_cost, 0, $max_xp_cost)", 
    "is_warp_stone -> damage_item(80)", 
    "is_inventory_button -> cooldown_cost('inventory_button', $inventory_button_cooldown)"
]

# List of variables used in the warpRequirements configuration.
warpSettings = [ 
    "$xp_per_block = 0.01", 
    "$min_xp_cost = 0", 
    "$max_xp_cost = 27", 
    "$interdimensional_xp_cost = 27", 
    "$inventory_button_cooldown = '300s'"
]

[worldGen]

# Approximate chunk distance between wild waystones being generated. Set to 0 to disable generation.
chunksBetweenWildWaystones = 25

# Set to 'preset_first' to first use names from the nameGenerationPresets. Set to 'preset_only' to use only those custom names. Set to 'mixed' to have some waystones use custom names, and others random names.
nameGenerationMode = "preset_first"

# These names will be used for the preset name generation mode. See the nameGenerationMode option for more info.
nameGenerationPresets = [  ]

# The template to use when generating new names. Supported placeholders are {Biome} (english biome name) and {MrPork} (the default name generator).
nameGenerationTemplate = "{MrPork}"

# Set to "regular" to have waystones spawn in some villages. Set to "frequent" to have waystones spawn in most villages. Set to "disabled" to disable waystone generation in villages. Waystones will only spawn in vanilla or supported villages.
spawnInVillages = "regular"

# Set to 'default' to only generate the normally textured waystones. Set to 'mossy' or 'sandy' to generate all as that variant. Set to 'biome' to make the style depend on the biome it is generated in.
wildWaystoneStyle = "biome"

# List of dimensions that wild waystones are allowed to spawn in. If left empty, all dimensions except those in wildWaystonesDimensionDenyList will be able to spawn waystones, provided the biomes are in the `has_structure/waystone` tag.
wildWaystonesDimensionAllowList = [ "minecraft:the_end", "minecraft:overworld", "minecraft:the_nether" ]

# List of dimensions that wild waystones are not allowed to spawn in, even if the biome is in the `has_structure/waystone` tag. Only used if wildWaystonesDimensionAllowList is empty.
wildWaystonesDimensionDenyList = [  ]
